WHY IT EXISTS

Sep 11 2026
is closer than it looks.

Most product teams in Europe first heard "CRA" at a trade show in 2025, read the Regulation once, and moved on. The enforcement date is now less than twelve months out. National market-surveillance authorities will ask for four things, and most product teams cannot answer any of them without weeks of scrambling.

F·01

"Show us your technical file"

CRA Article 27 requires a technical file made available to national market-surveillance authorities on request. Most product teams do not have one that a regulator would accept.

F·02

"Show us your SBOM"

Annex I requires a Software Bill of Materials per release. Most teams have a `package.json` or a `requirements.txt`. A regulator or downstream customer expects a signed SPDX + CycloneDX SBOM.

F·03

"Show us your vulnerability handling process"

Annex II requires a coordinated disclosure policy, 24-hour reporting of actively exploited vulnerabilities, and a defined patch SLA per severity. Most teams have "email us at security@" and hope.

F·04

"Show us your security-support lifecycle statement"

Article 10 requires purchase-time disclosure of the security-support end date + user-facing documentation of the update mechanism. Most product teams have not committed to a public support lifecycle.

WHO IT SERVES

EU manufacturers
of connected products in scope.

Any firm placing a "product with digital elements" on the EU market

The CRA scope is deliberately broad. If your product has firmware, connects to a network, or ships with software the buyer relies on, you are in scope. Non-EU manufacturers selling in the EU are in scope too, via the importer / authorised representative provisions.

Consumer IoT + smart home

Cameras, doorbells, hubs, lighting, appliances, wearables. The category with the most vendor-cloud-shutdown history and the highest CRA-scrutiny expected.

Industrial + commercial connected equipment

Sensors, controllers, HVAC gateways, energy monitors, POS terminals, kiosks. CRA Class II likely; higher-scrutiny conformity route.

Medical-adjacent connected devices

Connected devices that do not qualify as MDR-regulated medical devices: wellness wearables, tele-health accessories, in-home diagnostics. Dual regulatory posture (CRA + national health guidance).

Automotive + telematics components

Aftermarket connected components, fleet-telematics units, EV-charging hardware. CRA + Radio Equipment Directive + potentially UN R155.

01

Requirement-by-requirement mapping of your product against CRA Annex I essential requirements. Each requirement rated (compliant / partial / non-compliant) with specific evidence citations from your codebase, docs, and existing processes.

Annex II vulnerability handling assessment

Review of your current disclosure policy, patch SLA, bug bounty coverage, and CSIRT-reporting capability. Explicit gap list against Annex II obligations including the 24-hour actively-exploited-vuln reporting requirement.

Recommendation on Module A (internal control) vs Module H (full quality assurance) vs Notified Body engagement based on your product's classification (Important Product Class I / II or ordinary product with digital elements).

Prioritised remediation list ordered by regulatory exposure + implementation cost. Each item scoped in engineering weeks + € cost estimate. Each item is marked as deferrable to R·02 or required before Sep 11 2026.

Technical-file structure template

Template + sample outline for your CRA Article 27 technical file. Draws on the structure VF Empire published for VF Home + Guardian Shield + FileIT: real, regulator-facing documentation you can adapt.

06

90-minute presentation + 4-week Q&A window

Delivered on video call with your engineering + legal + product leads. Follow-up written Q&A over 4 weeks post-delivery. Included in the fixed fee.

COMMON QUESTIONS

What most first calls ask.

We're a non-EU manufacturer selling into the EU. Does CRA apply to us?

Yes. CRA applies to products placed on the EU market regardless of manufacturer origin. Non-EU manufacturers must either establish an EU authorised representative or work through an EU importer. The technical file + Declaration of Conformity requirements apply identically. We can help you structure the authorised-representative path.

We already have ISO 27001 / SOC 2 / cybersecurity insurance. Do we need CRA on top?

Yes. Those frameworks address information-security management for your organisation. CRA addresses the product placed on the market: its vulnerability handling, its SBOM, its security-support lifecycle. They complement rather than replace CRA obligations.

Can we skip CRA if our product is B2B only?

No. CRA applies to products placed on the EU market regardless of the buyer type. B2B products face the same essential requirements + vulnerability handling obligations. Class II classification is slightly more common for B2B industrial products, which means conformity assessment via a Notified Body may be required rather than self-attestation.

What if the audit reveals a gap we can't close by Sep 11 2026?

The remediation roadmap prioritises exactly this question. You'll get an honest assessment of what has to ship before enforcement + what can be phased. In some cases the answer is "delay the EU launch of this SKU until compliant". Better to hear that now than in December 2026 from a market-surveillance letter.

Do you handle the actual conformity-assessment paperwork?

The audit hands you the technical-file structure + Declaration of Conformity template + gap analysis. Filing paperwork with a Notified Body (for Module H) or maintaining the technical file (for Module A self-attestation) is a separate engagement; we quote it after the audit if you'd like us to continue.

Can you sign an NDA before the kick-off call?

Yes. We sign a standard mutual NDA within 24 hours of your request. If you have your own template we review + turn it around within 2 business days.

How do you handle payment?

Invoiced in EUR by VF Empire Corp Ltd (Malta VAT MT 2686-9431), payable by SEPA transfer. 50% at kick-off, 50% at deliverable. Payment via Noirda GmbH (Germany VAT DE...) if you require a German-invoice counterparty for VAT-recovery convenience.
